newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH declines comment on reported talks offer.
newsitem.headline: LVMH declines comment on reported talks offer.

text.p: LVMH declined to comment on Friday on a British newspaper report that Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc had made secret overtures to the French luxury goods and drinks group that could open the way to a merger of all three companies.

The Guardian newspaper reported on Friday that the British drinks groups Grand Met and Guinness had signalled they would be ready to hold top-level negotiations which could result in the inclusion of LVMH in their planned mega-merger.
"We have no comment on this article," a LVMH spokesman said.
LVMH has been buying Grand Met shares as part of an effort to block the proposed merger between Grand Met and Guinness in which it holds 14.2 percent.

So far it has acquired around 6.37 percent of the capital of Grand Met, spending 8.5 billion francs. LVMH is believed to be planning to keep buying Grand Met stock until it has acquired at least 10 percent at which point it could call an extraordinary shareholders' meeting.
Analysts expect LVMH chairman chairman Bernard Arnault to try to win enough allies in Grand Met to build up a 25 percent block to prevent the merger from going ahead.
His goal is to create a powerful drinks group combining all their brands.
LVMH shares rose on the back of the article in the Guardian, rising 3.25 percent to 1557 francs by 1201 GMT while the CAC-40 blue chip stock market index was down 2.27 percent.
LVMH shares had been weakening recently on investors fears' that its strategy was risky and expensive.
